title.raw: 卷47 列傳第39 藝術 Volume 47 Biographies 39: Artists

sentences.zh: 冀儁 蔣昇 姚僧垣 子最 黎景熙 趙文深 褚該

translations.literal: Ji Jun, Jiang Sheng, Yao Sengyuan, Zui, Li Jingxi, Zhao Wenshen, Chu Gai
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jun; Jiang Sheng; Yao Sengyuan; Yao Zui (his son); Li Jingxi; Zhao Wenshen; and Chu Gai

sentences.zh: 太祖受命之始，屬天下分崩，于時戎馬交馳，而學術之士蓋寡，故曲藝末技，咸見引納。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Taizu received the mandate, it happened that the realm was fragmented; at that time war-horses crossed paths swiftly, while men of learning were few—therefore minor arts and lesser skills were all brought in and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen first took power, the empire was falling apart. Armies clashed without pause, and learned men were scarce, so even minor crafts and humble skills found a welcome at court.

sentences.zh: 至若冀儁、蔣昇、趙文深之徒，雖才愧昔人，而名著當世。

translations.literal: As for men such as Ji Jun, Jiang Sheng, and Zhao Wenshen, though their talent fell short of the ancients, their fame was illustrious in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Ji Jun, Jiang Sheng, and Zhao Wenshen could not match the masters of old, yet they were famous in their own day.

sentences.zh: 及剋定鄢、郢，俊異畢集。

translations.literal: When Yan and Ying were captured and pacified, outstanding men gathered all together.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of Yan and Ying, men of exceptional ability flocked to court.

sentences.zh: 樂茂雅、蕭吉以陰陽顯，庾季才以天官稱，史元華相術擅奇，許奭、姚僧垣方藥特妙，斯皆一時之美也。

translations.literal: Yue Maoya and Xiao Ji became illustrious through yin-yang lore; Yu Jicai was famed for astral affairs; Shi Yuanhua was uniquely skilled in physiognomy; Xu Yi and Yao Sengyuan were singularly excellent in prescriptions and medicines—these were all the finest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Maoya and Xiao Ji won renown through yin-yang lore; Yu Jicai was known for astral affairs; Shi Yuanhua was unmatched in physiognomy; Xu Yi and Yao Sengyuan were singularly skilled in medicine and prescriptions—all were the finest of their time.

sentences.zh: 茂雅、元華、許奭，史失其傳。

translations.literal: Maoya, Yuanhua, and Xu Yi—the histories have lost their accounts.
translations.idiomatic: For Maoya, Yuanhua, and Xu Yi, the histories preserve no biographies.

sentences.zh: 季才、蕭吉，官成於隋。

translations.literal: Jicai and Xiao Ji completed their official careers under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Jicai and Xiao Ji finished their careers in office under the Sui dynasty.

sentences.zh: 自餘紀於此篇，以備遺闕云爾。

translations.literal: The rest are recorded in this chapter to supply what would otherwise be missing.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder are set down in this chapter so that nothing is left out.

sentences.zh: 冀儁字僧儁，太原陽邑人也。

translations.literal: Ji Jun, courtesy name Sengjun, was a native of Yangyi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Jun, whose courtesy name was Sengjun, came from Yangyi in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 性沉謹，善隸書，特工模寫。

translations.literal: By nature he was reserved and careful; he excelled at clerical script and was especially skilled at imitation copying.
translations.idiomatic: He was reserved and meticulous by nature, excelled at clerical script, and was especially gifted at copying documents by hand.

sentences.zh: 魏太昌初，為賀拔岳墨曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang of Wei, he served as Recorder of Ink for Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taichang era of Wei, he served as recorder in the ink office under Heba Yue.

sentences.zh: 及岳被害，太祖引為記室。

translations.literal: When Yue was killed, Taizu took him on as recording secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue was murdered, Emperor Wen brought him on as recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 時侯莫陳悅阻兵隴右，太祖志在平之。

translations.literal: At that time Houmochen Yue was holding out with troops in Longyou; Taizu was intent on pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Houmochen Yue was defying the court with an army in Longyou, and Emperor Wen was determined to crush him.

sentences.zh: 乃令儁偽為魏帝勅書與費也頭，令將兵助太祖討悅。

translations.literal: He then had Jun forge an imperial edict of the Wei emperor to the Feiye Tou, ordering them to lead troops to assist Taizu in attacking Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He had Jun forge an imperial edict from the Wei emperor to the Feiye Tou tribe, ordering them to march and help Emperor Wen attack Yue.

sentences.zh: 儁依舊勅模寫，及代舍人、主書等署，與真無異。

translations.literal: Jun copied according to old edicts, and also forged the signatures of attendants, chief clerks, and the like—there was no difference from the genuine.
translations.idiomatic: Jun copied from genuine edicts and forged the signatures of palace attendants and chief clerks as well, so that the document was indistinguishable from the real thing.

sentences.zh: 太祖大悅。

translations.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was delighted.

sentences.zh: 費也頭已曾得魏帝敕書，及見此勅，不以為疑。

translations.literal: The Feiye Tou had previously received edicts from the Wei emperor; when they saw this edict, they did not regard it with suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: The Feiye Tou had received Wei imperial edicts before; when they saw this one, they never suspected a forgery.

sentences.zh: 遂遣步騎一千，受太祖節度。

translations.literal: They then sent a thousand infantry and cavalry, subject to Taizu's command.
translations.idiomatic: They duly sent a thousand foot and horse soldiers to serve under Emperor Wen's command.

sentences.zh: 大統初，除丞相府城局參軍，封長安縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Datong, he was appointed Army Bureau Adjutant in the Chancellor's Office, enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Datong era he was made adjutant in the army bureau of the chancellor's office and enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 從復弘農，戰沙苑，進爵為子，出為華州中正。

translations.literal: He followed in the recovery of Hongnong and fought at Shayuan, was advanced in rank to viscount, and went out as Rectifier of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the recovery of Hongnong and the battle at Shayuan, was raised to viscount, and was sent out as provincial rectifier for Hua.

sentences.zh: 十三年，遷襄樂郡守。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was transferred to be Administrator of Xiangyue Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to serve as administrator of Xiangyue commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋征教世宗及宋獻公等隸書。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to teach clerical script to Shizong and Duke Xian of Song and others.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon summoned to instruct Emperor Ming and Duke Xian of Song and others in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 時俗入書學者，亦行束修之禮，謂之謝章。

translations.literal: At the time the custom for those entering the study of writing was also to perform the ceremony of bundled silk, called the 'letter of thanks.'
translations.idiomatic: At the time students of calligraphy still observed the ceremony of presenting bundled silk to their teacher, which was called the letter of thanks.

sentences.zh: 儁以書字所興，起自蒼頡，若同常俗，未為合禮。

translations.literal: Jun held that writing arose from Cangjie; to treat it like ordinary custom was not in accord with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued that writing itself originated with Cangjie, and that treating calligraphy like an ordinary craft did not accord with proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 遂啟太祖，釋奠蒼頡及先聖、先師。

translations.literal: He then memorialized Taizu to offer the libation sacrifice to Cangjie as well as to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Emperor Wen to offer libation sacrifices to Cangjie as well as to the Former Sage and Former Teacher.

sentences.zh: 除黃門侍郎、本州大中正。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Grand Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed attendant at the yellow gate and grand rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 累遷撫軍將軍、右金紫光祿大夫、都督、通直散騎常侍、車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army, Right Grand Master of the Golden Gate and Purple Radiance, Commander, Regular Attendant of the Unimpeded Cavalry, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to general who pacifies the army, right grand master of the golden gate and purple radiance, commander, regular attendant of the unimpeded cavalry, general of chariots and cavalry, and palace attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗二年，以本官為大使，巡歷州郡，察風俗，理冤滯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shizong, with his existing office he served as grand envoy, touring the provinces and commanderies, inspecting customs, and settling grievances left unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming's reign he served as imperial envoy at his existing rank, touring the provinces to inspect local customs and clear backlogged grievances.

sentences.zh: 還，拜小御正。

translations.literal: On his return, he was appointed Junior Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he was appointed junior imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 尋出為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Governor of Hu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as governor of Hu province.

sentences.zh: 性退靜，每以清約自處，前後所歷，頗有聲稱。

translations.literal: By nature he was retiring and quiet; he always conducted himself with frugality and integrity, and in every post he held he won a fair reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring and quiet by nature, he always lived modestly and with integrity, and wherever he served he earned a solid reputation.

sentences.zh: 尋加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，改封昌樂縣伯。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional titles of General of Agile Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the First Rank with an office equal to the Three Excellencies, and his enfeoffment was changed to Earl of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made general of agile cavalry and palace attendant of the first rank with an office equal to the three excellencies, and his title was changed to Earl of Changle.

sentences.zh: 又進爵為侯，增邑幷前一千六百戶。

translations.literal: He was further advanced to marquis, and his fief was increased to a total of one thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was further raised to marquis, with his fief increased to a total of sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 蔣昇字鳳起，楚國平河人也。

translations.literal: Jiang Sheng, courtesy name Fengqi, was a native of Pinghe in the state of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Sheng, whose courtesy name was Fengqi, came from Pinghe in the state of Chu.

sentences.zh: 父儁，魏南平王府從事中郎、趙興郡守。

translations.literal: His father Jun served as Attendant Gentleman of the Prince of Nanping's household in Wei and as Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun had served as attendant gentleman in the household of the Prince of Nanping under Wei and as administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 昇性恬靜，少好天文玄象之學。

translations.literal: Sheng was tranquil by nature and from youth loved the study of astronomy and arcane celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was calm and retiring by nature and from youth devoted himself to astronomy and celestial lore.

sentences.zh: 太祖雅信待之，常侍左右，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Taizu trusted and treated him with great regard, keeping him constantly at his side to serve as adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen trusted him deeply and kept him constantly at his side as a consultant.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，東魏將竇泰入寇，濟自風陵，頓軍潼關。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, the Eastern Wei general Dou Tai invaded; he crossed from Fengling and encamped his army at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong the Eastern Wei general Dou Tai invaded, crossed at Fengling, and encamped at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 太祖出師馬牧澤。

translations.literal: Taizu led his army out from Muma Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen marched out from Muma Marsh.

sentences.zh: 時西南有黃紫氣抱日，從未至酉。

translations.literal: At that time in the southwest there was yellow and purple vapor embracing the sun, from the hour wei until the hour you.
translations.idiomatic: At the time yellow and purple vapors in the southwest embraced the sun from mid-afternoon until evening.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂昇曰：「此何祥也？

translations.literal: Taizu said to Sheng, "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked Sheng, "What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 」昇曰：「西南未地，主土。

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "The southwest is the wei quarter, which governs earth.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "The southwest is the wei quarter, which governs earth.

sentences.zh: 土王四季，秦之分也。

translations.literal: Earth is king in all four seasons; this is the allotment of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Earth dominates through all four seasons, and this is the region of Qin.

sentences.zh: 今大軍旣出，喜氣下臨，必有大慶。

translations.literal: Now that the great army has marched forth and auspicious vapor descends from above, there is sure to be a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Our main force is already in the field and auspicious vapor descends upon us—there will surely be a great triumph.

sentences.zh: 」於是進軍與竇泰戰，擒之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he advanced and fought Dou Tai, capturing him.
translations.idiomatic: The army then advanced, fought Dou Tai, and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 自後遂降河東，剋弘農，破沙苑。

translations.literal: Afterward they successively pacified Hedong, captured Hongnong, and broke through Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they pacified Hedong, took Hongnong, and won at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 由此愈被親禮。

translations.literal: From this he was ever more treated with intimacy and honor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was treated with ever greater favor and respect.

sentences.zh: 九年，高仲密以北豫州來附。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Gao Zhongmi came over with North Yuzhou to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Gao Zhongmi defected with North Yuzhou to join the Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲遣兵援之，又以問昇。

translations.literal: Taizu wished to send troops to aid him and again consulted Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen wanted to send troops to support him and again asked Sheng's opinion.

sentences.zh: 昇對曰：「春王在東，熒惑又在井、鬼之分，行軍非便。

translations.literal: Sheng replied, "The spring king is in the east, and Mars is again in the quarters of Jing and Gui—marching troops would not be advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng replied, "The spring king is in the east, and Mars is in the Well and Ghost constellations—it would be unwise to march.

sentences.zh: 」太祖不從，軍遂東行。

translations.literal: " Taizu did not follow this advice, and the army then marched east.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen did not heed him, and the army marched east.

sentences.zh: 至邙山，不利而還。

translations.literal: When they reached Mount Mang, the outcome was unfavorable and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: At Mount Mang the campaign went badly and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太師賀拔勝怒，白太祖曰：「蔣昇罪合萬死。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng was angry and reported to Taizu, "Jiang Sheng deserves death ten thousand times over.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Heba Sheng was furious and told Emperor Wen, "Jiang Sheng deserves death ten thousand times over.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「蔣昇固諫，云出師不利。

translations.literal: " Taizu said, "Jiang Sheng firmly remonstrated, saying that taking the army forth would be unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "Jiang Sheng urged me firmly that the campaign would go badly.

sentences.zh: 此敗也，孤自取之，非昇過也。」

translations.literal: This defeat—I brought it on myself; it is not Sheng's fault."
translations.idiomatic: This defeat I brought on myself. It is not Sheng's fault."

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，以前後功，授車騎大將軍、儀同三司，封高城縣子，邑五百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei, in recognition of his services before and after, he was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank, enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaocheng with a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was made general of chariots and cavalry and palace attendant of the third rank for his services, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Gaocheng with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 保定二年，增邑三百戶，除河東郡守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoding, his fief was increased by three hundred households, and he was appointed Administrator of Hedong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoding his fief was increased by three hundred households and he was appointed administrator of Hedong commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋入為太史中大夫。

translations.literal: Soon he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Imperial Astrologer.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled to the capital as grand master of the imperial astrologer.

sentences.zh: 以老請致仕，詔許之。

translations.literal: On grounds of age he requested retirement, and an edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on account of age, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 加定州刺史。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title of Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of governor of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 姚僧垣字法衛，吳興武康人，吳太常信之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Yao Sengyuan, courtesy name Fawei, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing, the eighth-generation descendant of Yao Xin, Grand Master of Ceremonies of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sengyuan, whose courtesy name was Fawei, came from Wukang in Wuxing and was the eighth-generation descendant of Yao Xin, grand master of ceremonies under Wu.

sentences.zh: 曾祖郢，宋員外散騎常侍、五城侯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ying was Attendant Cavalier at Large of the Song and Marquis of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ying had been attendant cavalier at large under the Song and marquis of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 父菩提，梁高平令。

translations.literal: His father Puti was Magistrate of Gaoping under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Puti had served as magistrate of Gaoping under the Liang.

sentences.zh: 嘗嬰疾歷年，乃留心醫藥。

translations.literal: He had once suffered illness for years and therefore devoted himself to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: After years of illness he turned his attention to medicine.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝性又好之，每召菩提討論方術，言多會意，由是頗禮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang was also fond of this by nature; he often summoned Puti to discuss prescriptions and techniques, and his words often hit the mark—therefore he was quite honored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang also loved medicine and often summoned Puti to discuss prescriptions; Puti's answers usually struck home, and the emperor treated him with considerable respect.

sentences.zh: 僧垣幼通洽，居喪盡禮。

translations.literal: Sengyuan was broadly learned from youth and observed mourning rites to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan was widely learned from childhood and observed mourning rites scrupulously.

sentences.zh: 年二十四，卽傳家業。

translations.literal: At twenty-four he already inherited the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-four he had already taken up the family profession of medicine.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝召入禁中，面加討試。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang summoned him into the inner palace and tested him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu summoned him to the inner palace and examined him in person.

sentences.zh: 僧垣酬對無滯。

translations.literal: Sengyuan answered without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan answered without a moment's hesitation.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝甚奇之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang marveled at him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 大通六年，解褐臨川嗣王國左常侍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Datong, he left the commoner's garb as Left Regular Attendant in the kingdom of the Heir of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Datong he entered office as left regular attendant in the kingdom of the heir of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，除驃騎廬陵王府田曹參軍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong, he was appointed Field Bureau Adjutant in the household of the Prince of Luling, General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he was made field bureau adjutant in the household of the Prince of Luling, general of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 九年，還領殿中醫師。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was again placed in charge as Palace Physician.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was again placed in charge as palace physician.

sentences.zh: 時武陵王所生葛修華，宿患積時，方術莫效。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Xiuhua, birth mother of the Prince of Wuling, had a chronic ailment of long standing, and no prescription or technique had effect.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ge Xiuhua, birth mother of the Prince of Wuling, had suffered a chronic illness for years, and no treatment had helped.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝乃令僧垣視之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang then ordered Sengyuan to examine her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu then sent Sengyuan to examine her.

sentences.zh: 還，具說其狀，幷記增損時候。

translations.literal: On his return he fully described her condition and also recorded the times of improvement and decline.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he described her condition in full and noted precisely when her symptoms waxed and waned.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝歎曰：「卿用意綿密，乃至於此，以此候疾，何疾可逃。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang sighed and said, "Your attention is so meticulous as to reach this degree—with such observation of illness, what illness could escape?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu exclaimed, "Your attention to detail is extraordinary. With such close observation of an illness, what disease could possibly escape notice?

sentences.zh: 朕常以前代名人，多好此術，是以每恒留情，頗識治體。

translations.literal: I have often noted that famous men of former ages were fond of this art, and therefore I have always paid attention to it and know something of the principles of treatment.
translations.idiomatic: I have often noticed that famous men of former ages loved this art, and I have always paid it close attention and learned something of how to treat disease.

sentences.zh: 今聞卿說，益開人意。

translations.literal: Now hearing your explanation opens my understanding all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing you speak today has opened my understanding even further.

sentences.zh: 」十一年，轉領太醫正，加文德主帥、直合將軍。

translations.literal: " In the eleventh year he was transferred to head the office of Chief Imperial Physician, with the additional titles of Commander of Wende and General of the Direct Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made chief imperial physician, with the additional titles of commander of Wende and general of the direct guard.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝嘗因發熱，欲服大黃。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang once, because of fever, wished to take rhubarb.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu once had a fever and wanted to take rhubarb.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「大黃乃是快藥。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said, "Rhubarb is a purgative drug.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "Rhubarb is a strong purgative.

sentences.zh: 然至尊年高，不宜輕用。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty is advanced in years and should not use it lightly.
translations.idiomatic: But Your Majesty is advanced in years and should not use it lightly.

sentences.zh: 」帝弗從，遂至危篤。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not follow this, and the illness thereupon reached a critical state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed him, and his condition soon became critical.

sentences.zh: 梁簡文帝在東宮，甚禮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Jian of Liang, when he was in the Eastern Palace, treated him with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jian of Liang was crown prince, he treated Sengyuan with great respect.

sentences.zh: 四時伏臘，每有賞賜。

translations.literal: At the seasonal festivals of summer and winter, he always received rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer and winter festivals he always received gifts from the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太清元年，轉鎮西湘東王府中記室參軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiqing, he was transferred to be Recording Secretary in the household of the Prince of Xiangdong, General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiqing he was transferred to recording secretary in the household of the Prince of Xiangdong, general who guards the west.

sentences.zh: 僧垣少好文史，不留意於章句。

translations.literal: Sengyuan from youth loved literature and history and did not concern himself with textual glosses.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Sengyuan loved literature and history and cared little for textual commentary.

sentences.zh: 時商略今古，則為學者所稱。

translations.literal: When he discussed and weighed past and present, he was praised by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: When he discussed affairs ancient and modern, scholars praised his insight.

sentences.zh: 及侯景圍建業，僧垣乃棄妻子赴難。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing besieged Jianye, Sengyuan abandoned wife and children to go to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing besieged Jianye, Sengyuan left his wife and children behind and rushed to the capital's defense.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝嘉之，授戎昭將軍、湘東王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang commended this and appointed him General of Martial Brilliance and Recording Secretary in the household of the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu commended his loyalty and appointed him general of martial brilliance and recording secretary in the household of the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 及宮城陷，百官逃散。

translations.literal: When the palace city fell, the hundred officials fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace fell, officials fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 僧垣假道歸，至吳興，謁郡守張

translations.literal: Sengyuan took a roundabout route home, reaching Wuxing, and called on the prefect Zhang
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan made his way home by a detour. When he reached Wuxing, he called on the prefect Zhang

translations.literal: (Rong)
translations.idiomatic: Rong (variant character; standard form: Sheng)

translations.literal: [Sheng].
translations.idiomatic: Sheng.

sentences.zh: 嵊見僧垣流涕曰：「吾過荷朝恩，今報之以死。

translations.literal: Sheng, seeing Sengyuan, wept and said, "I have received more than my share of grace from the court; now I repay it with my death.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng saw Sengyuan he wept and said, "The court has shown me more favor than I deserve; now I will repay that debt with my life.

sentences.zh: 君是此邦大族，又朝廷舊臣。

translations.literal: You are a great clan of this region and also a former minister of the court.
translations.idiomatic: You are a leading family of this region and a former minister of the court.

sentences.zh: 今日得君，吾事辦矣。

translations.literal: Today, having obtained you, my affair is accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have come, my purpose can be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」俄而景兵大至，攻戰累日，郡城遂陷。

translations.literal: " Before long Jing's troops arrived in force; fighting went on for days, and the commandery seat fell.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hou Jing's army arrived in strength. After days of fighting the commandery seat fell.

sentences.zh: 僧垣竄避久之，乃被拘執。

translations.literal: Sengyuan fled and hid for a long time before he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan went into hiding for a long time before he was captured.

sentences.zh: 景將侯子鑒素聞其名，深相器遇，因此獲免。

translations.literal: Jing's general Hou Zijian had long heard of his reputation and held him in high regard, and for this reason he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing's general Hou Zijian had long heard of his fame and treated him with great respect, which is how he escaped execution.

sentences.zh: 及梁簡文嗣位，僧垣還建業，以本官兼中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jian of Liang succeeded to the throne, Sengyuan returned to Jianye and held his former office concurrently with Attendant Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jian of Liang came to the throne, Sengyuan returned to Jianye and served in his former post while also acting as drafting secretary in the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子鑒尋鎮廣陵，僧垣又隨至江北。

translations.literal: Zijian soon took up his post at Guangling, and Sengyuan followed him north of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Zijian was soon posted to Guangling, and Sengyuan followed him to the north bank of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝平侯景，召僧垣赴荊州，改授晉安王府諮議。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he summoned Sengyuan to Jingzhou and reassigned him as Adviser in the household of the Prince of Jin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang defeated Hou Jing, he summoned Sengyuan to Jingzhou and made him adviser in the household of the Prince of Jin'an.

sentences.zh: 其時雖剋平大亂，而任用非才，朝政混淆，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: Although the great disorder had then been quelled, unworthy men were employed, court affairs were confused, and order was no longer maintained.
translations.idiomatic: Although the great rebellion had been put down, the wrong men held office, government was in confusion, and discipline had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 僧垣每深憂之。

translations.literal: Sengyuan was deeply troubled by this each time.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan was deeply troubled whenever he saw this.

sentences.zh: 謂故人曰：「吾觀此形勢，禍敗不久。

translations.literal: He said to an old friend, "Looking at this situation, disaster and defeat are not far off.
translations.idiomatic: He told an old friend, "Judging from the way things stand, ruin is not far away.

sentences.zh: 今時上策，莫若近關。

translations.literal: The best course now would be to draw near to the passes."
translations.idiomatic: The wisest move now would be to get close to the frontier passes."

sentences.zh: 」聞者皆掩口竊笑。

translations.literal: Those who heard this all covered their mouths and laughed in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him covered their mouths and laughed behind his back.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝嘗有心腹疾，乃召諸醫議治療之方。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang once suffered from a visceral ailment and summoned the physicians to discuss methods of treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan once suffered a disorder of the internal organs and summoned physicians to discuss treatment.

sentences.zh: 咸謂至尊至貴，不可輕脫，宜用平藥，可漸宣通。

translations.literal: All said that His Majesty was supremely exalted and must not be purged lightly; mild medicines should be used to bring gradual relief.
translations.idiomatic: They all said the emperor was too exalted to be purged aggressively and that mild medicines should be used for gradual relief.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「脈洪而實，此有宿食。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said, "The pulse is surging and full—this indicates long-standing undigested food.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "The pulse is surging and full. This means there is old undigested food in the stomach.

sentences.zh: 非用大黃，必無差理。

translations.literal: Unless rhubarb is used, there will be no way to cure it."
translations.idiomatic: Without rhubarb there is no hope of a cure."

sentences.zh: 」梁元帝從之，進湯訖，果下宿食，因而疾愈。

translations.literal: " Emperor Yuan followed this; after the decoction was taken, the old food was indeed expelled and the illness was cured.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan followed his advice. After the decoction was taken the stagnant food passed and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝大喜。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan was delighted.

sentences.zh: 時初鑄錢，一當十，乃賜錢十萬，實百萬也。

translations.literal: At that time new coin was first cast, each piece counting as ten, and he was rewarded with one hundred thousand coins—in real value, one million.
translations.idiomatic: New coin had just been minted at ten to the old unit, and he was given one hundred thousand pieces—worth a million in real terms.

sentences.zh: 金州刺史伊婁穆以疾還京，請僧垣省疾。

translations.literal: Yi Loumu, Governor of Jin Province, returned to the capital because of illness and asked Sengyuan to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Loumu, governor of Jin province, returned to the capital ill and asked Sengyuan to examine him.

sentences.zh: 乃云：「自腰至臍，似有三縛，兩腳緩縱，不復自持。

translations.literal: He said, "From the waist to the navel it is as though there are three bindings; both legs are slack and can no longer support themselves."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "From my waist to my navel it feels as though I am bound in three places, and both legs are so weak they can barely hold me up."

sentences.zh: 」僧垣為診脈，處湯三劑。

translations.literal: " Sengyuan took his pulse and prescribed three doses of decoction.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan took his pulse and prescribed three doses of decoction.

sentences.zh: 穆初服一劑，上縛卽解；

translations.literal: When Mu took the first dose, the upper binding was immediately released;
translations.idiomatic: After the first dose the upper binding was gone;

sentences.zh: 次服一劑，中縛復解；

translations.literal: when he took the second dose, the middle binding was also released;
translations.idiomatic: after the second the middle binding released as well;

sentences.zh: 又服一劑，三縛悉除。

translations.literal: when he took the third dose, all three bindings were entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: and after the third all three bindings were gone.

sentences.zh: 而兩腳疼痹，猶自攣弱。

translations.literal: Yet both legs were painful and numb and still weak and contracted.
translations.idiomatic: His legs were still painful and numb and remained weak.

sentences.zh: 更為合散一劑，稍得屈申。

translations.literal: He then prepared another dose of powder compound, and the limbs gradually regained flexion and extension.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan then gave him a powder compound, and his legs gradually regained their strength.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「終待霜降，此患當愈。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said, "In the end one must wait until frost descends; then this ailment will be cured."
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "You must wait until the frost comes; then this illness will be cured."

sentences.zh: 」及至九月，遂能起行。

translations.literal: " When the ninth month came, he was able to rise and walk.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month he could rise and walk again.

sentences.zh: 大將軍、襄樂公賀蘭隆先有氣疾，加以水腫，喘息奔急，坐臥不安。

translations.literal: Helan Long, Grand General and Duke of Xiangle, had long suffered from a qi disorder, with edema added; he panted in haste and could neither sit nor lie at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Helan Long, grand general and Duke of Xiangle, had long suffered from a qi disorder complicated by edema; he gasped for breath and could find no rest sitting or lying down.

sentences.zh: 或有勸其服決命大散者，其家疑未能決，乃問僧垣。

translations.literal: Some urged him to take the fatal great dispersing powder; his family hesitated and could not decide, and so they asked Sengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to take the powerful dispersing powder known as the fatal dose; his family could not decide and asked Sengyuan.

sentences.zh: 僧垣曰：「意謂此患不與大散相當。

translations.literal: Sengyuan said, "In my view this ailment is not suited to the great dispersing powder.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan said, "In my view this illness is not suited to that great dispersing powder.

sentences.zh: 若欲自服，不煩賜問。

translations.literal: If you wish to take it on your own, there is no need to ask me."
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to take it anyway, you need not ask me."

sentences.zh: 」因而委去。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: With that he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 其子殷勤拜請曰：「多時抑屈，今日始來。

translations.literal: His son bowed earnestly and pleaded, "For a long time we held you back; only today have you come.
translations.idiomatic: His son bowed earnestly and said, "We held you back too long; only today have you come.

sentences.zh: 竟不可治，意實未盡。

translations.literal: If in the end you cannot treat him, our wish is still not fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you cannot cure him in the end, we have not yet done all we can."

sentences.zh: 」僧垣知其可差，卽為處方，勸使急服。

translations.literal: " Sengyuan knew he could be cured and at once prescribed medicine, urging him to take it quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan knew he could be cured, prescribed at once, and urged them to take it quickly.

sentences.zh: 便卽氣通，更服一劑，諸患悉愈。

translations.literal: Immediately his breathing cleared; after one more dose all his ailments were cured.
translations.idiomatic: His breathing cleared at once; after one more dose all his ailments were gone.

sentences.zh: 建德三年，文宣太后寢疾，醫巫雜說，各有異同。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiande, Empress Dowager Wenxuan fell ill; physicians and shamans offered mixed and contradictory explanations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiande Empress Dowager Wenxuan fell ill, and physicians and shamans gave conflicting diagnoses.

sentences.zh: 高祖御內殿，引僧垣同坐，曰：「太后患勢不輕，諸醫並云無慮。

translations.literal: Gaozu received him in the inner hall and seated Sengyuan beside him, saying, "The empress dowager's condition is grave; all the physicians say there is no cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu received him in the inner hall and seated Sengyuan beside him. "The empress dowager is gravely ill," he said, "yet all the physicians tell me not to worry.

sentences.zh: 朕人子之情，可以意得。

translations.literal: As a son, my feelings may be guessed.
translations.idiomatic: As her son, you can imagine what I feel.

sentences.zh: 君臣之義，言在無隱。

translations.literal: Between ruler and minister, the rule is that nothing should be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and minister there must be no concealment.

sentences.zh: 公為何如？

translations.literal: What is your view?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣無聽聲視色之妙，特以經事已多，准之常人，竊以憂懼。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant has no miraculous gift of hearing pulses or reading faces; but having seen many cases, judging by ordinary people, I venture to feel apprehensive."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have no miraculous gift for reading pulses or faces, but I have seen many cases, and compared with ordinary patients I am afraid for her."

sentences.zh: 」帝泣曰：「公旣決之矣，知復何言！

translations.literal: " The emperor wept and said, "Since you have already decided, what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "Since you have already decided, what more can I say?"

sentences.zh: 」尋而太后崩。

translations.literal: " Before long the empress dowager died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the empress dowager died.

sentences.zh: 其後復因召見，帝問僧垣曰：「姚公為儀同幾年？

translations.literal: Later, on being summoned again, the emperor asked Sengyuan, "How many years has Lord Yao held the rank of Palace Attendant?"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor asked him, "How long have you held the rank of palace attendant, Lord Yao?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣忝荷朝恩，於茲九載。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant has received grace from the court for nine years now."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have borne the court's favor for nine years now."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「勤勞有日，朝命宜隆。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "Your long service deserves a loftier appointment from the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your long service deserves a higher appointment."

sentences.zh: 」乃授驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the First Rank with an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made general of agile cavalry and palace attendant of the first rank with an office equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 又敕曰：「公年過縣車，可停朝謁。

translations.literal: An edict also said, "You have passed the age of seventy; you may cease attending court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also said, "You are past seventy; you may stop coming to court.

sentences.zh: 若非別勅，不勞入見。」

translations.literal: Unless there is a special order, you need not come in to see me."
translations.idiomatic: Unless I summon you specially, you need not attend."

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖親戎東討，至河陰遇疾。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Gaozu personally led an eastern campaign; when he reached Heyin he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Emperor Wu led a campaign east and fell ill at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 口不能言；

translations.literal: He could not speak;
translations.idiomatic: He could not speak;

translations.literal: (face)
translations.idiomatic: face

sentences.zh: 〔瞼〕垂覆目，不復瞻視；

translations.literal: [eyelids] drooped and covered his eyes, and he could no longer see;
translations.idiomatic: his eyelids drooped over his eyes so that he could no longer see;

sentences.zh: 一足短縮，又不得行。

translations.literal: one foot was shortened and contracted, and he could not walk.
translations.idiomatic: one foot was shortened and he could not walk.

sentences.zh: 僧垣以為諸藏俱病，不可並治。

translations.literal: Sengyuan held that all the viscera were afflicted and could not be treated together.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan judged that all the viscera were affected and could not be treated at once.

sentences.zh: 軍中之要，莫先於語。

translations.literal: Of what is vital in the army, nothing comes before speech.
translations.idiomatic: In an army on campaign, the ability to speak comes first.

sentences.zh: 乃處方進藥，帝遂得言。

translations.literal: He then prescribed medicine and administered it, and the emperor was able to speak.
translations.idiomatic: He prescribed medicine, and the emperor recovered his speech.

sentences.zh: 次又治目，目疾便愈。

translations.literal: Next he treated the eyes, and the eye ailment was at once cured.
translations.idiomatic: Next he treated his eyes, and the eye ailment was cured.

sentences.zh: 末乃治足，足疾亦瘳。

translations.literal: Last he treated the foot, and the foot ailment was also healed.
translations.idiomatic: Last he treated his foot, and that too was healed.

sentences.zh: 比至華州，帝已痊復。

translations.literal: By the time they reached Hua Province, the emperor had fully recovered.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they reached Hua province the emperor had fully recovered.

sentences.zh: 卽除華州刺史，仍詔隨入京，不令在鎮。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Governor of Hua Province, but an edict ordered him to follow into the capital and not remain at his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Hua province but ordered to follow the emperor to the capital and not remain in office there.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年，表請致仕，優詔許之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuanzheng he memorialized requesting retirement, and a gracious edict granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuanzheng he asked to retire, and a gracious edict approved.

sentences.zh: 是歲，高祖行幸雲陽，遂寢疾。

translations.literal: That year Gaozu traveled to Yunyang and there fell gravely ill.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Wu traveled to Yunyang and fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 乃詔僧垣赴行在所。

translations.literal: He then ordered Sengyuan to come to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Sengyuan to come to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 內史柳

translations.literal: Palace Secretary Liu
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretary Liu

translations.literal: (Sheng)
translations.idiomatic: Sheng

sentences.zh: 〔昂〕私問曰：「至尊貶膳日久，脈候何如？

translations.literal: [Ang] asked him privately, "His Majesty has eaten little for many days—how is his pulse?"
translations.idiomatic: Ang asked him privately, "His Majesty has eaten little for many days. How is his pulse?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「天子上應天心，或當非愚所及。

translations.literal: " He replied, "The Son of Heaven corresponds to Heaven's heart; perhaps it is not for a fool like me to judge.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "The Son of Heaven is sustained by Heaven itself; perhaps that is beyond my judgment.

sentences.zh: 若凡庶如此，萬無一全。

translations.literal: If an ordinary man were in such a state, not one in ten thousand would survive."
translations.idiomatic: If an ordinary man were in such a state, not one in ten thousand would survive."

sentences.zh: 」尋而帝崩。

translations.literal: " Before long the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 宣帝初在東宮，常苦心痛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan was first in the Eastern Palace, he often suffered heart pain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan was crown prince he often suffered from heart pain.

sentences.zh: 乃令僧垣治之，其疾卽愈。

translations.literal: He had Sengyuan treat it, and the ailment was at once cured.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan treated him and the ailment was cured at once.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，恩禮彌隆。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, favor and honor were ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to the throne his favor and honor only grew.

sentences.zh: 常從容謂僧垣曰：「常聞先帝呼公為姚公，有之乎？

translations.literal: He once said to Sengyuan at leisure, "I have often heard that the former emperor called you Lord Yao—is that so?"
translations.idiomatic: He once asked Sengyuan at leisure, "I have often heard that my father called you Lord Yao. Is that true?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣曲荷殊私，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: " He replied, "Your servant has received extraordinary favor, and it is indeed as Your Majesty says."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have received extraordinary favor, and it is exactly as Your Majesty says."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此是尚齒之辭，非為貴爵之號。

translations.literal: " The emperor said, "That was a term of respect for age, not a title of noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That was a term of respect for your age, not a noble title.

sentences.zh: 朕當為公建國開家，為子孫永業。

translations.literal: I shall establish a state and open a house for you, an estate for your descendants forever."
translations.idiomatic: I shall establish a fief and a house for you, an estate your descendants may hold forever."

sentences.zh: 」乃封長壽縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was then enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Changshou with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 冊命之日，又賜以金帶及衣服等。

translations.literal: On the day of the investiture he was also given a gold belt, garments, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his investiture he also received a gold belt, garments, and the like.

sentences.zh: 大象二年，除太醫下大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang he was appointed Grand Master of the Lower Imperial Physicians.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daxiang he was appointed grand master of the lower imperial physicians.

sentences.zh: 帝尋有疾，至于大漸。

translations.literal: The emperor soon fell ill and reached the final crisis.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon fell gravely ill and neared death.

sentences.zh: 僧垣宿直侍。

translations.literal: Sengyuan kept night watch in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan kept night watch at his bedside.

sentences.zh: 帝謂隨公曰：「今日性命，唯委此人。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Duke Sui, "Today my life is entrusted to this man alone."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Duke Sui, "Today my life rests in this man's hands alone."

sentences.zh: 」僧垣知帝診候危殆，必不全濟。

translations.literal: Sengyuan knew the emperor's condition was perilous and that he could not be fully saved.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan knew the emperor's condition was hopeless and that he could not be saved.

sentences.zh: 乃對曰：「臣荷恩旣重，思在效力。

translations.literal: He therefore replied, "Your servant has received grace so heavy that my thought is to exert my strength.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have received such great favor that I mean to do all I can.

sentences.zh: 但恐庸短不逮，敢不盡心。

translations.literal: Yet I fear my mediocrity and shortcoming will not suffice—I dare not fail to give my utmost."
translations.idiomatic: But I fear my abilities are too slight; still, I dare not hold anything back."

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 及靜帝嗣位，遷上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, Sengyuan was promoted to Grand General of the Palace Attendant of the First Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jing succeeded to the throne, Sengyuan was promoted to grand general of the palace attendant of the first rank.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，進爵北絳郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang under Sui, he was advanced to Duke of Beijiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang under the Sui he was raised to Duke of Beijiang.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，時年八十五。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, aged eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 遺誡衣白帢入棺，朝服勿斂。

translations.literal: He left instructions to be buried in white headcloth and not to be dressed in court robes.
translations.idiomatic: He left instructions to wear white headcloth in the coffin and not to be dressed in court robes.

sentences.zh: 靈上唯置香奩，每日設清水而已。

translations.literal: On the bier only an incense casket was placed; each day only clear water was set out.
translations.idiomatic: On the bier only an incense casket was placed, with fresh water set out each day.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加荊、湖二州刺史。

translations.literal: His former office was posthumously conferred, with the additional titles of Governor of Jing and Hu provinces.
translations.idiomatic: His former office was posthumously confirmed and he was given the additional titles of governor of Jing and Hu provinces.

sentences.zh: 僧垣醫術高妙，為當世所推。

translations.literal: Sengyuan's medical art was sublime and subtle and was esteemed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan's medical skill was superb and won the esteem of his age.

sentences.zh: 前後效驗，不可勝記。

translations.literal: Cases in which his treatment proved effective cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The cases in which his treatment succeeded are too many to record.

sentences.zh: 聲譽旣盛，遠聞邊服。

translations.literal: His reputation grew ever greater and was heard far on the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: His fame spread until it reached the frontier regions.

sentences.zh: 至於諸蕃外域，咸請託之。

translations.literal: Even the various barbarian lands beyond the borders all sought to entrust themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Even foreign peoples beyond the borders sought his care.

sentences.zh: 僧垣乃搜采奇異，參校徵效者，為《集驗方》十二卷，又撰《行記》三卷，行於世。

translations.literal: Sengyuan then searched out marvelous cases, collated those with proven effect, and made twelve scrolls of Collected Proven Prescriptions; he also composed three scrolls of Travel Records, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan collected remarkable cases, verified those that had proved effective, and compiled twelve scrolls of Collected Proven Prescriptions, along with three scrolls of Travel Records, both of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 長子察在江南。

translations.literal: His eldest son Cha was in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Cha remained in the south.

sentences.zh: 次子最，字士會，幼而聰敏，及長，博通經史，尤好著述。

translations.literal: The second son Zui, courtesy name Shihui, was clever from childhood; when grown he broadly mastered the classics and histories and especially loved writing.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Zui, courtesy name Shihui, was clever as a boy and, when he grew up, mastered the classics and histories; he especially loved to write.

sentences.zh: 年十九，隨僧垣入關。

translations.literal: At nineteen he followed Sengyuan in entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he followed his father west through the passes.

sentences.zh: 世宗盛聚學徒，校書於麟趾殿，最亦預為學士。

translations.literal: Shizong greatly gathered students and collated books at Linzhi Hall; Zui also took part as a scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming gathered many students to collate books at Linzhi Hall, and Zui served among them as a scholar.

sentences.zh: 俄授齊王憲府水曹參軍，掌記室事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Water Bureau Adjutant in the household of Prince Xian of Qi, in charge of recording-secretary affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made water bureau adjutant in the household of Prince Xian of Qi and managed the recording secretariat.

sentences.zh: 特為憲所禮接，賞賜隆厚。

translations.literal: He was especially treated with courtesy by Xian, and rewards and gifts were generous and thick.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian treated him with special courtesy and lavished generous gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，憲以嫌疑被誅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Xian was executed on suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Xian was executed on suspicion of treason.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝作相，追復官爵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui served as chancellor, he posthumously restored his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was still chancellor, he restored Xian's offices and titles posthumously.

sentences.zh: 最以陪遊積歲，恩顧過隆，乃錄憲功績為傳，送上史局。

translations.literal: Zui had accompanied him in pleasure outings for years and received excessive favor; he therefore compiled a biography of Xian's achievements and submitted it to the historiography office.
translations.idiomatic: Having accompanied Xian for years and received extraordinary favor, Zui compiled a biography of his achievements and submitted it to the historiography office.

sentences.zh: 最幼在江左，迄于入關，未習醫術。

translations.literal: Zui from childhood had been in the Jiang left; until entering the passes he had not studied medical art.
translations.idiomatic: Zui had grown up in the south and had not studied medicine before entering the passes.

sentences.zh: 天和中，齊王憲奏高祖，遣最習之。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era Prince Xian of Qi memorialized Gaozu, requesting that Zui study it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era Prince Xian memorialized Emperor Wu, asking that Zui be trained in medicine.

sentences.zh: 憲又謂最曰：「爾博學高才，何如王褒、庾信。

translations.literal: Xian also said to Zui, "You are broadly learned and of high talent—how do you compare with Wang Bao and Yu Xin?
translations.idiomatic: Xian also told him, "You are learned and gifted. How do you compare with Wang Bao and Yu Xin?

sentences.zh: 王、庾名重兩國，吾視之蔑如。

translations.literal: Wang and Yu were famous in both states; I regard them as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Yu were famous in both the Liang and the Northern Zhou, but I think nothing of them.

sentences.zh: 接待資給，非爾家比也。

translations.literal: The reception and support given you cannot be compared with their families.
translations.idiomatic: The welcome and support you receive from me are unlike anything they ever had.

sentences.zh: 爾宜深識此意，勿不存心。

translations.literal: You should deeply understand this intent and not fail to keep it in mind.
translations.idiomatic: You must take this to heart and never forget it.

sentences.zh: 且天子有敕，彌須勉勵。

translations.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven has issued an edict—you must strive all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself has ordered it, so you must work all the harder.

sentences.zh: 」最於是始受家業。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zui first received the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: With that Zui began to learn the family art of medicine.

sentences.zh: 十許年中，略盡其妙。

translations.literal: Within some ten years he had broadly mastered its subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Within about ten years he had mastered its essentials.

sentences.zh: 每有人造請，效驗甚多。

translations.literal: Whenever people came to consult him, the cures were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever patients came to him, his treatments proved effective again and again.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝踐極，除太子門大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui took the throne, Zui was appointed grand master of the crown prince's gate.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去官，哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's mourning and was so grief-stricken that only skin and bone remained.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father and grieved until he was skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 旣免喪，襲爵北絳郡公，復為太子門大夫。

translations.literal: When mourning was ended, he inherited the title Duke of Beijiang and again became Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he inherited the title Duke of Beijiang and returned to his post as grand master of the crown prince's gate.

sentences.zh: 俄轉蜀王秀友。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Friend of Prince Xiu of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to be friend of Prince Xiu of Shu.

sentences.zh: 秀鎮益州，遷秀府司馬。

translations.literal: Xiu was posted to Yizhou and Zui was promoted to be marshal of Xiu's princely household.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu was posted to Yizhou, Zui was made marshal of his princely household.

sentences.zh: 及平陳，察至。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, Cha arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen dynasty fell, his brother Cha arrived from the south.

sentences.zh: 最自以非嫡，讓封于察，隋文帝許之。

translations.literal: Zui, considering himself not the eldest son, yielded the enfeoffment to Cha, and Emperor Wen of Sui approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Zui, knowing he was not the eldest son, yielded the title to Cha, and Emperor Wen approved.

sentences.zh: 秀後陰有異謀，隋文帝令公卿窮治其事。

translations.literal: Later Xiu secretly harbored rebellious designs; Emperor Wen of Sui ordered the high ministers to investigate the matter thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiu secretly plotted rebellion, and Emperor Wen ordered a full investigation by the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 開府慶整、郝偉等並推過於秀。

translations.literal: Palace Attendants Qing Zheng, Hao Wei, and others all shifted blame onto Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants Qing Zheng, Hao Wei, and others all tried to shift blame onto Xiu.

sentences.zh: 最獨曰：「凡有不法，皆最所為，王實不知也。

translations.literal: Only Zui said, "Whatever was unlawful was done by me; the prince truly did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zui said, "Whatever was unlawful, I did it; the prince truly knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 」搒訊數百，卒無異辭。

translations.literal: " After hundreds of beatings under interrogation, in the end his words did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He was beaten hundreds of times under interrogation but never changed his story.

sentences.zh: 最竟坐誅。

translations.literal: Zui in the end was punished with execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zui was executed in the end.

sentences.zh: 時年六十七。

translations.literal: He was sixty-seven years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 論者義之。

translations.literal: Commentators praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Later commentators praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 撰《梁後略》十卷，行於世。

translations.literal: He composed ten scrolls of Epitome of the Later Liang, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ten scrolls of Epitome of the Later Liang, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 黎景熙字季明，河間

translations.literal: Li Jingxi, courtesy name Jiming, was a native of Hejian
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxi, courtesy name Jiming, came from Hejian

translations.literal: (Zheng)
translations.idiomatic: Mo

sentences.zh: 〔鄚〕人也，少以字行於世。

translations.literal: of Mo; from youth he was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: a native of Mo county; from youth he was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 曾祖嶷，魏太武時，從破平涼，有功，賜爵容城縣男，加鷹揚將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ni, in the time of Emperor Taiwu of Wei, followed in the capture of Pingliang and had merit; he was granted the title Baron of Rongcheng and given the additional title General of Soaring Hawk.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ni, under Emperor Taiwu of Wei, took part in the capture of Pingliang and was rewarded with the title Baron of Rongcheng and the additional rank of general of soaring hawk.

sentences.zh: 後為燕郡守。

translations.literal: Later he became Administrator of Yan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as administrator of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖鎮，襲爵，為員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen inherited the title and served as Attendant Cavalier at Large.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen inherited the title and served as attendant cavalier at large.

sentences.zh: 父瓊，太和中，襲爵，歷員外郎、魏縣令，後至鄜城郡守。

translations.literal: His father Qiong, in the Taihe era, inherited the title and passed through the posts of Attendant Gentleman and Magistrate of Wei County, later reaching Administrator of Fucheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiong inherited the title in the Taihe era and rose through attendant gentleman and magistrate of Wei county to administrator of Fucheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 季明少好讀書，性強記默識，而無應對之能。

translations.literal: Jiming from youth loved reading; he had a strong memory and silent retention but no ability in repartee.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jiming loved books; he remembered silently and retained much, but was awkward in conversation.

sentences.zh: 其從祖廣，太武時為尚書郎，善古學。

translations.literal: His paternal uncle Guang, in the time of Emperor Taiwu, was a Gentleman in the Masters of Writing and was skilled in ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal uncle Guang, under Emperor Taiwu, was a gentleman in the masters of writing and excelled in ancient learning.

sentences.zh: 嘗從吏部尚書清河崔玄伯受字義，又從司徒崔浩學楷篆，自是家傳其法。

translations.literal: He once received instruction in the meaning of characters from Cui Xuanbo of Qinghe, Minister of Personnel, and also studied regular and seal script from Minister of State Cui Hao—thereafter the family transmitted this method.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the meaning of characters under Cui Xuanbo, minister of personnel, and regular and seal script under Minister of State Cui Hao; the family thereafter transmitted these arts.

sentences.zh: 季明亦傳習之，頗與許氏有異。

translations.literal: Jiming also received and practiced them, differing somewhat from the Xu school.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming learned them too, though his tradition differed somewhat from the Xu school.

sentences.zh: 又好占玄象，頗知術數。

translations.literal: He also loved divining the arcane signs of heaven and knew something of numerology.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved celestial divination and knew something of numerology.

sentences.zh: 而落魄不事生業。

translations.literal: Yet he was down and out and did not pursue a livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lived in poverty and did not pursue a regular livelihood.

sentences.zh: 有書千餘卷。

translations.literal: He had more than a thousand scrolls of books.
translations.idiomatic: He owned more than a thousand scrolls of books.

sentences.zh: 雖窮居獨處，不以饑寒易操。

translations.literal: Though he dwelt in poverty alone, he did not change his principles because of hunger or cold.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lived alone in poverty, hunger and cold never changed his principles.

sentences.zh: 與范陽盧道源為莫逆之友。

translations.literal: He and Lu Daoyuan of Fanyang were friends of the closest bond.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lu Daoyuan of Fanyang were the closest of friends.

sentences.zh: 永安中，道源勸令入仕，始為威烈將軍。

translations.literal: In the Yongan era Daoyuan urged him to enter office; he first became General of Majestic Valor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongan era Daoyuan urged him into office; he first became general of majestic valor.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武初，遷鎮遠將軍，尋除步兵校尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei he was promoted to General Who Extends Far and soon appointed Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was promoted to general who extends far and soon made colonel of footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，季明乃寓居伊、洛。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Jiming then took up residence in the Yi and Luo region.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Jiming settled in the Yi and Luo region.

sentences.zh: 侯景徇地河外，召季明從軍。

translations.literal: Hou Jing overran the lands beyond the Yellow River and summoned Jiming to join his army.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing overran the lands beyond the Yellow River and summoned Jiming to his army.

sentences.zh: 尋授銀青光祿大夫，加中軍將軍，拜行臺郎中，除黎陽郡守。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Grand Master of the Silver Gate and Purple Radiance, promoted to General of the Center Army, appointed Attendant Gentleman on the Mobile Staff, and made Administrator of Liyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the title grand master of the silver gate and purple radiance, made general of the center army, appointed attendant gentleman on the mobile staff, and named administrator of Liyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 季明從至懸瓠，察景終不足恃，遂去之。

translations.literal: Jiming followed to Xuanhu, perceived that Jing in the end could not be relied on, and then left him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming followed him to Xuanhu, saw that Hou Jing could not be trusted, and left.

sentences.zh: 客於潁川，以世路未清，欲優遊卒歲。

translations.literal: He lodged in Yingchuan, and because the age's path was not yet clear, wished to pass the year in ease.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed in Yingchuan and, finding the times unsettled, hoped to live out the year in peace.

sentences.zh: 時王思政鎮潁川，累使召。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Sizheng was defending Yingchuan and repeatedly sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was then defending Yingchuan and summoned him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 季明不得已，出與相見。

translations.literal: Jiming had no choice but to go out and meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming had no choice but to go and see him.

sentences.zh: 留于內館月餘。

translations.literal: He was kept in the inner lodge for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: He was kept in the inner lodge for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 太祖又徵之，遂入關。

translations.literal: Taizu also summoned him, and he then entered the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen also summoned him, and he entered the passes.

sentences.zh: 乃令季明正定古今文字於東閤。

translations.literal: He was then ordered to fix and determine ancient and modern writing in the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to standardize ancient and modern writing in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 大統末，除安西將軍，尋拜著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Datong he was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and soon made Assistant Gentleman for Composition.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Datong he was made general who pacifies the west and soon assistant gentleman for composition.

sentences.zh: 於時倫輩，皆位兼常伯，車服華盛。

translations.literal: At that time his peers all held concurrent posts as regular palace attendants, with splendid carriages and robes.
translations.idiomatic: His peers all held concurrent posts as regular palace attendants and dressed in splendid style.

sentences.zh: 唯季明獨以貧素居之，而無愧色。

translations.literal: Only Jiming lived in plain poverty without a look of shame.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jiming lived plainly and without shame.

sentences.zh: 又勤於所職，著述不怠。

translations.literal: He was also diligent in his duties and never slackened in writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent in his duties and never slackened in his writing.

sentences.zh: 然性尤專固，不合於時。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was especially stubborn and inflexible, not in harmony with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stubborn by nature and ill suited to the times.

sentences.zh: 是以一為史官，遂十年不調。

translations.literal: Therefore once he became a historiographer, he went ten years without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became a historiographer, he went ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝元年，進號平南將軍、右銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the South and Right Grand Master of the Silver Gate and Purple Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was promoted to general who pacifies the south and right grand master of the silver gate and purple radiance.

sentences.zh: 六官建，為外史上士。

translations.literal: When the Six Offices were established, he became Senior Clerk in the Outer Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: When the six offices were established he became senior clerk in the outer historiography.

sentences.zh: 孝閔帝踐阼，加征南將軍、右金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended the throne, he was given the additional titles General Who Campaigns South and Right Grand Master of the Golden Gate and Purple Radiance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne he received the additional titles general who campaigns south and right grand master of the golden gate and purple radiance.

sentences.zh: 時大司馬賀蘭祥討吐谷渾，詔季明從軍。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Marshal Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, and an edict ordered Jiming to follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Jiming was ordered to accompany the army.

sentences.zh: 還，除驃騎將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and Right Grand Master of Radiant Honor.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made general of agile cavalry and right grand master of radiant honor.

sentences.zh: 武成末，遷外史下大夫。

translations.literal: At the end of Wucheng he was promoted to Lower Grand Master of the Outer Historiography.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wucheng era he was promoted to lower grand master of the outer historiography.

sentences.zh: 保定三年，盛營宮室。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, palace construction was carried out on a grand scale.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Baoding palace construction was carried out on a grand scale.

sentences.zh: 春夏大旱，詔公卿百寮，極言得失。

translations.literal: In spring and summer there was great drought; the emperor ordered the high ministers and hundred officials to speak to the utmost on gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and summer brought severe drought, and the emperor ordered the high ministers to speak freely on what was going wrong.

sentences.zh: 季明上書曰：

translations.literal: Jiming submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞成湯遭旱，以六事自陳。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed himself in six matters.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when Cheng Tang encountered drought, he confessed his faults in six matters.

sentences.zh: 宣王太甚，而珪璧斯竭。

translations.literal: When King Xuan went too far, jade disks and bi were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When King Xuan of Zhou went too far, even jade offerings were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 豈非遠慮元元，俯哀兆庶。

translations.literal: Was this not because he looked far to the common people and bowed in pity to the masses?
translations.idiomatic: Surely that was because he looked to the welfare of the people and pitied the masses.

sentences.zh: 方今農要之月，時雨猶愆，率土之心，有懷渴仰。

translations.literal: Now in the month when agriculture is vital, timely rain is still lacking; the heart of all within the realm thirsts and looks up.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the month when agriculture matters most, timely rain is still lacking, and the whole realm looks up in thirst.

sentences.zh: 陛下垂情萬類，子愛羣生，覲禮百神，猶未豐洽者，豈或作事不節，有違時令，舉措失中，儻邀斯旱。

translations.literal: Your Majesty extends affection to the ten thousand kinds and loves the multitude as children; you observe rites toward the hundred spirits, yet abundance is not yet full—could it be that works are not regulated, the seasons are violated, or measures are misplaced, perchance inviting this drought?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty cares for all living things and loves the people as his children; you perform rites to the spirits, yet blessings are not complete. Could it be that undertakings are ill timed, the seasons violated, or measures misplaced, and so this drought has been invited?

sentences.zh: 《春秋》，君舉必書，動為典禮，水旱陰陽，莫不應行而至。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that a ruler's every act must be written; movement is canon and ritual—flood, drought, yin and yang, none fail to respond to conduct and arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records every act of a ruler; conduct is canon and ritual, and flood, drought, and the balance of yin and yang all respond to how a ruler behaves.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「言行，君子之所以動天地，可不慎乎。

translations.literal: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Words and conduct are how the gentleman moves Heaven and Earth—can one not be cautious?

sentences.zh: 」《春秋》莊公三十一年冬，不雨。

translations.literal: " The Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Zhuang year 31 winter: no rain.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that in the thirty-first year of Duke Zhuang of Lu, winter, there was no rain.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》以為是歲一年而三築臺，奢侈不恤民也。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year platforms were built three times in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year three platforms were built in one year—extravagance without pity for the people.

sentences.zh: 僖公二十一年夏，大旱。

translations.literal: Duke Xi year 21 summer: great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Duke Xi of Lu, summer, there was great drought.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》以為時作南門，勞民興役。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was being built, laboring the people with corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that at that time the southern gate was under construction, exhausting the people with labor.

sentences.zh: 漢惠帝二年夏，大旱。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Han year 2 summer: great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Hui of Han, summer, there was great drought.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，大旱，江河水少，溪澗水絕。

translations.literal: Year 5 summer: great drought; the Yangtze and Yellow rivers had little water, and streams and brooks dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, summer, there was great drought; the great rivers ran low and streams dried up.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》以為先是發民十四萬六千人城長安。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that before this 146,000 men had been mobilized to build the walls of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 漢武帝元狩三年夏，大旱。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han, Yuanshou year 3 summer: great drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanshou of Emperor Wu of Han, summer, there was great drought.

sentences.zh: 五行傳以為是歲發天下故吏穿昆明池。

translations.literal: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year men throughout the realm who had formerly held office were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on the Five Phases holds that in that year former officials throughout the realm were mobilized to dig the Kunming Pool.

sentences.zh: 然則土木之功，動民興役，天輒應之以異。

translations.literal: Thus works of earth and wood, moving the people with corvée—Heaven always responds with anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus whenever earth and wood works mobilize the people, Heaven responds with anomalies.

sentences.zh: 典籍作誡，儻或可思。

translations.literal: The admonitions of the classics—perhaps they may be pondered.
translations.idiomatic: The warnings of the classics are perhaps worth pondering.

sentences.zh: 上天譴告，改之則善。

translations.literal: Heaven's reproof—if changed, then good.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's reproof, if heeded, leads to good.

sentences.zh: 今若息民省役，以答天譴，庶靈澤時降，嘉谷有成，則年登可覬，子來非晚。

translations.literal: If now the people are rested and corvée reduced, to answer Heaven's reproof, then perhaps timely blessings will descend, fine grain will ripen, the year's harvest may be hoped for, and the people will come as children—not late.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty now rests the people and reduces corvée to answer Heaven's reproof, timely rain may fall, grain ripen, and the people come gladly—not too late.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「民亦勞止，迄可小康。

translations.literal: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "The people also have labored; let them have a little ease.

sentences.zh: 惠此中國，以綏四方。

translations.literal: Show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."
translations.idiomatic: Show favor to this central kingdom to bring peace to the four quarters."

sentences.zh: 」或恐極陽生陰，秋多雨水，年復不登，民將無覬。

translations.literal: " Or perhaps one fears that when yang reaches its extreme yin is born, and in autumn there will be much rain; the year again will not yield, and the people will have nothing to hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Or perhaps when yang reaches its extreme, yin will arise; autumn may bring heavy rain, the harvest may fail again, and the people will have nothing to hope for.

sentences.zh: 如又薦饑，為慮更甚。

translations.literal: If famine is added on top, the concern is even greater.
translations.idiomatic: If famine follows as well, the danger is even greater.

sentences.zh: 時豪富之家，競為奢麗。

translations.literal: At that time wealthy and powerful families vied in extravagant luxury.
translations.idiomatic: At the time wealthy families competed in extravagant display.

sentences.zh: 季明又上書曰：

translations.literal: Jiming again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted another memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞寬大所以兼覆，慈愛所以懷眾。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that breadth and largeness are what enable covering all; kindness and love are what enable embracing the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that breadth enables covering all, and kindness enables embracing the multitude.

sentences.zh: 故天地稱其高厚者，萬物得其容養焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive their shelter and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and Earth are called high and thick because the ten thousand things receive shelter and nurture from them.

sentences.zh: 四時著其寒暑者，庶類資其忠信焉。
