translations.literal: The four seasons display their cold and heat because the myriad kinds rely on their constancy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: The four seasons show cold and heat because all living kinds rely on their constancy and good faith.

sentences.zh: 是以帝王者，寬大象天地，忠信則四時。

translations.literal: Thus emperors and kings take Heaven and Earth as their model of breadth, and the four seasons as their constancy and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Thus emperors and kings model themselves on the breadth of Heaven and Earth and the good faith of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 招搖東指，天下識其春。

translations.literal: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows it is spring.
translations.idiomatic: When the Dipper points east, all under Heaven knows spring has come.

sentences.zh: 人君布德，率土懷其惠。

translations.literal: When a ruler spreads virtue, all within the realm cherishes his grace.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler spreads virtue, the realm cherishes his grace.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下資乾御寓，品物咸亨，時乘六龍，自強不息，好問受規，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Bow low: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs the realm; all things flourish. You ride the six dragons, strengthen yourself without cease, love to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, endowed with Heaven's potency, governs all things in prosperity, rides the six dragons without cease, and loves to ask and receive remonstrance—the realm is greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 自古至治之君，亦皆廣延博訪，詢采芻蕘，置喜樹木，以求其過。

translations.literal: From antiquity well-governed rulers have all broadly extended invitations and sought counsel, gathering even the words of grass cutters, setting up boards to welcome criticism, to seek out their faults.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity well-governed rulers have sought counsel widely, even from the humblest, and welcomed criticism to learn their faults.

sentences.zh: 頃年亢旱踰時，人懷望歲。

translations.literal: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season; people harbored hope for the year's harvest.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years drought lasted beyond its season, and the people hoped for rain.

sentences.zh: 陛下爰發明詔，廣求人瘼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty then issued a brilliant edict, broadly seeking the people's afflictions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty issued a brilliant edict seeking the people's afflictions.

sentences.zh: 同禹、湯之罪己，高宋景之守正。

translations.literal: This matches Yu and Tang in blaming themselves and rises to Song Jing in holding to the upright.
translations.idiomatic: This matched Yu and Tang in blaming themselves and Song Jing in holding to the upright.

sentences.zh: 澍雨應時，年穀斯稔。

translations.literal: Timely rain responded; the year's grain ripened.
translations.idiomatic: Timely rain came; the year's grain ripened.

sentences.zh: 剋己節用，慕質惡華，此則尚矣。

translations.literal: Restraining oneself and economizing, admiring simplicity and detesting splendor—this is already lofty.
translations.idiomatic: You restrained yourself and economized, admired simplicity and detested extravagance—this is already lofty.

sentences.zh: 然而朱紫仍耀於衢路，綺縠猶侈於豪家；

translations.literal: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, and fine silks are still extravagant in great houses;
translations.idiomatic: Yet crimson and purple still blaze on the roads, and fine silks still adorn great houses;

sentences.zh: 裋褐未充於細民，糟糠未厭於編戶。

translations.literal: coarse cloth does not fill the common people, and chaff and husks do not satisfy registered households.
translations.idiomatic: coarse cloth does not clothe the common people, and coarse grain does not fill their bowls.

sentences.zh: 此則勸導之理有所未周故也。

translations.literal: This is because the principle of guidance and leading has not yet been fully applied.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that guidance and persuasion have not yet reached everywhere.

sentences.zh: 今雖導之以政，齊之以刑，風俗固難以一矣。

translations.literal: Now though you guide them with government and align them with punishments, custom is hard to make one.
translations.idiomatic: Though you guide them with government and align them with punishments, custom is hard to unify at once.

sentences.zh: 昔文帝集上書之囊，以作帷帳；

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered the bags of memorials to make curtains;
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han gathered memorial bags to make curtains;

sentences.zh: 惜十家之產，不造露臺；

translations.literal: he prized the wealth of ten households and would not build the open terrace;
translations.idiomatic: he would not build a terrace that cost the wealth of ten households;

sentences.zh: 後宮所幸，衣不曳地，方之今日富室之飾，曾不如婢隸之服。

translations.literal: those favored in the rear palace wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with the adornment of rich houses today, they were not even like servants' dress.
translations.idiomatic: palace women wore robes that did not trail on the ground—compared with rich houses today, even servants dress more lavishly.

sentences.zh: 然而以身率下，國富刑清，廟稱太宗，良有以也。

translations.literal: Yet by taking the body to lead those below, the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple calls him Emperor Taizong—and rightly so.
translations.idiomatic: By leading through his own example the state grew rich and punishments were clear; the temple honors him as Emperor Taizong, and rightly so.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人久於其道，而天下化成。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage long abides in the Way, all under Heaven is transformed.

sentences.zh: 今承魏氏喪亂之後，貞信未興。

translations.literal: Now, inheriting the age after Wei's disorders, constancy and trust have not yet arisen.
translations.idiomatic: Now, after the disorders of Wei, constancy and trust have not yet been restored.

sentences.zh: 宜先「遵五美，屏四惡」，革浮華之俗，抑流競之風，察鴻都之小藝，焚雉頭之異服，無益之貨勿重於時，虧德之器勿陳於側，則民知德矣。

translations.literal: One should first "follow the five beauties and banish the four evils," reform the custom of empty show, restrain the wind of reckless competition, examine the minor arts of Hongdu, burn the strange garments of pheasant-head style, let goods of no benefit not be prized in the age, and vessels that harm virtue not be displayed at the side—then the people will know virtue.
translations.idiomatic: First follow the five beauties and banish the four evils: reform empty display, restrain reckless competition, examine minor arts, burn outlandish dress, let useless goods not be prized, and harmful luxuries not be displayed—then the people will know virtue.

sentences.zh: 臣又聞之，為治之要，在於選舉。

translations.literal: Your servant has also heard that the essential of governing lies in selection and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The essential of governing lies in selection and appointment.

sentences.zh: 若差之毫釐，則有千里之失。

translations.literal: If there is a hairsbreadth of error, there will be a thousand-li mistake.
translations.idiomatic: A hairsbreadth of error leads to a thousand-li mistake.

sentences.zh: 後來居上，則致積薪之譏。

translations.literal: If later comers take precedence, it brings the reproach of piled firewood.
translations.idiomatic: If later comers take precedence, it brings the reproach of piled firewood.

sentences.zh: 是以古之善為治者，貫魚以次，任必以能。

translations.literal: Therefore those skilled in governing in antiquity arranged them like strung fish in order and always assigned office according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers skilled in governing ranked men in order and assigned office by ability.

sentences.zh: 爵人於朝，不以私愛。

translations.literal: When ennobling men at court, they did not act from private affection.
translations.idiomatic: When ennobling men at court they did not act from private affection.

sentences.zh: 簡材以授其官，量能以任其用。

translations.literal: They selected talent to grant office and measured capacity to assign use.
translations.idiomatic: They selected talent for office and measured capacity for use.

sentences.zh: 官得其材，用當其器，六轡旣調，坐致千里。

translations.literal: Office obtained its talent, use matched its vessel; once the six reins were adjusted, sitting still one reached a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Office obtained talent and use matched capacity; once the reins were adjusted, one could reach a thousand li while sitting still.

sentences.zh: 虞、舜選眾，不仁者遠。

translations.literal: Yu and Shun selected from the multitude, and the unkind were far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Shun selected from the multitude, and the unkind stood far off.

sentences.zh: 則庶事康哉，民知其化矣。

translations.literal: Then the myriad affairs were at peace and the people knew transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Then the myriad affairs were at peace and the people knew transformation.

sentences.zh: 帝覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and commended it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it and commended it.

sentences.zh: 時外史廨宇屢移，未有定所。

translations.literal: At that time the offices of the outer historiography had been moved repeatedly and had no fixed place.
translations.idiomatic: The outer historiography offices had been moved repeatedly and had no fixed site.

sentences.zh: 季明又上言曰：「外史之職，漢之東觀，儀等石渠，司同天祿。

translations.literal: Jiming again submitted, saying, "The office of outer historiography in Han was the Eastern Pavilion, its ritual equal to Shiqu, its charge the same as Tianlu.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted again: "The outer historiography in Han was the Eastern Pavilion, equal in ritual to Shiqu and in charge to Tianlu.

sentences.zh: 是乃廣內秘府，藏言之奧。

translations.literal: This is the broad inner secret repository, the mystery of stored words.
translations.idiomatic: It is the broad inner secret repository, the mystery of stored words.

sentences.zh: 帝王所寶，此焉攸在。

translations.literal: What emperors and kings treasure resides here.
translations.idiomatic: What emperors and kings treasure resides here.

sentences.zh: 自魏及周，公館不立。

translations.literal: From Wei through Zhou, the public offices were not established.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei through Zhou the public offices were not established.

sentences.zh: 臣雖愚瞽，猶知其非，是以去年十一月中，敢冒陳奏。

translations.literal: Your servant, though foolish and blind, still knows this is wrong; therefore in the eleventh month of last year I dared to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am foolish, I know this is wrong; therefore last eleventh month I dared memorialize.

sentences.zh: 將降中旨，卽遣修營。

translations.literal: An edict was about to descend from the center, and construction was immediately dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was about to descend and construction was ordered.

sentences.zh: 荏苒一周，未加功力。

translations.literal: A full year has passed without added labor.
translations.idiomatic: A full year has passed without progress.

sentences.zh: 臣職思其憂，敢不重請。

translations.literal: Your servant's office broods on its worry and dares to request again.
translations.idiomatic: My office broods on this and dares request again.

sentences.zh: 」帝納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 於是廨宇方立。

translations.literal: Thereupon the office buildings were established.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the office buildings were established.

sentences.zh: 天和三年，進車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianhe he was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianhe he was promoted to general of chariots and cavalry and palace attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 趙文深字德本，南陽宛人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Wenshen, courtesy name Deben, was a native of Wan in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wenshen, courtesy name Deben, came from Wan in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 父遐，以醫術進，仕魏為尚藥典御。

translations.literal: His father Xia advanced through medical art and served Wei as Director of Imperial Medicines.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xia advanced through medicine and served Wei as director of imperial medicines.

sentences.zh: 文深少學楷隸，年十一，獻書於魏帝。

translations.literal: Wenshen from youth studied regular and clerical script; at eleven he presented writing to the Wei emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen studied regular and clerical script from youth; at eleven he presented his writing to the Wei emperor.

sentences.zh: 立義歸朝，除大丞相府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: When righteousness was established and he returned to the court, he was appointed Law Bureau Adjutant in the Grand Chancellor's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When he submitted to the court he was appointed law bureau adjutant in the grand chancellor's office.

sentences.zh: 文深雅有鐘、王之則，筆勢可觀。

translations.literal: Wenshen elegantly had the norms of Zhong and Wang; his brush momentum was admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen had the standards of Zhong You and Wang Xizhi; his brushwork was admirable.

sentences.zh: 當時碑牓，唯文深及冀儁而已。

translations.literal: At the time for steles and tablets, only Wenshen and Ji Jun were considered.
translations.idiomatic: At the time only Wenshen and Ji Jun were considered for steles and tablets.

sentences.zh: 大統十年，追論立義功，封白石縣男，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Datong, in recognition of his merit in establishing righteousness, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Baishi with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Datong he was enfeoffed as Baron of Baishi with a fief of two hundred households for his merit in submitting to the court.

sentences.zh: 太祖以隸書紕繆，命文深與黎季明、沉遐等依《說文》及《字林》刊定六體，成一萬餘言，行於世。

translations.literal: Taizu, because clerical script was erroneous, ordered Wenshen together with Li Jiming, Shen Xia, and others to collate the six scripts according to the Shuowen and Zilin, making more than ten thousand characters, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Because clerical script was erroneous, Emperor Wen ordered Wenshen, Li Jiming, Shen Xia, and others to collate the six scripts according to the Shuowen and Zilin, producing more than ten thousand characters that circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 及平江陵之後，王褒入關，貴遊等翕然並學褒書。

translations.literal: After the pacification of Jiangling, Wang Bao entered the passes, and the noble wanderers all at once studied Bao's writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangling was pacified, Wang Bao entered the passes and the elite all studied his calligraphy at once.

sentences.zh: 文深之書，遂被遐棄。

translations.literal: Wenshen's writing was then cast far off.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen's calligraphy was then cast aside.

sentences.zh: 文深慚恨，形於言色。

translations.literal: Wenshen's shame and resentment showed in his words and face.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshen's shame and resentment showed in his words and face.

sentences.zh: 後知好尚難反，亦攻習褒書，然竟無所成，轉被譏議，謂之學步邯鄲焉。

translations.literal: Later knowing that preferences are hard to reverse, he also attacked and studied Bao's writing, yet in the end achieved nothing and was turned to ridicule, called one who learns the Handan walk.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing that taste could not be reversed, he tried to study Bao's style too, but achieved nothing and was mocked as one who learns the Handan walk.

sentences.zh: 至於碑牓，餘人猶莫之逮。

translations.literal: As for steles and tablets, others still could not match him.
translations.idiomatic: In steles and tablets, others still could not match him.

sentences.zh: 王褒亦每推先之。

translations.literal: Wang Bao also always put him first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bao always ranked him first as well.

sentences.zh: 宮殿樓閣，皆其跡也。

translations.literal: Palaces, towers, and pavilions—all bear his traces.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces, towers, and pavilions all bear his inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 遷縣伯下大夫，加儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Lower Grand Master of a district earl and given the additional title Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to lower grand master of a district earl and given palace attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 世宗令至江陵書景福寺碑，漢南人士，亦以為工。

translations.literal: Shizong ordered him to go to Jiangling to write the stele of Jingfu Temple; men of south of the Han also considered it skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming ordered him to Jiangling to write the stele of Jingfu Temple; men south of the Han also praised his skill.

sentences.zh: 梁主蕭詧觀而美之，賞遺甚厚。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler Xiao Cha viewed it and admired it, rewarding and sending gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler Xiao Cha admired it and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 天和元年，露寢等初成，文深以題牓之功，增邑二百戶，除趙興郡守。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianhe, when the open sleeping quarters and the like were first completed, Wenshen because of the merit of inscribing tablets was given an increased fief of two hundred households and appointed Administrator of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianhe, when new palace buildings were completed, Wenshen was given two hundred more households for inscribing tablets and appointed administrator of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 文深雖外任，每須題牓，輒復追之。

translations.literal: Though Wenshen served outside, whenever tablets needed inscription he was again summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served outside office, whenever an inscription was needed he was summoned back.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 褚該字孝通，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Chu Gai, courtesy name Xiaotong, was a native of Yangzhai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Gai, courtesy name Xiaotong, came from Yangzhai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 晉末，遷居江左。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin he moved to settle in the Jiang left.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jin his family moved to the south.

sentences.zh: 祖長樂，齊竟陵王錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Changle was Recording Secretary in the household of the Prince of Jingling of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Changle was recording secretary in the household of the Prince of Jingling of Qi.

sentences.zh: 父義昌，梁鄱陽王中記室。

translations.literal: His father Yichang was Recording Secretary in the household of the Prince of Poyang of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yichang was recording secretary in the household of the Prince of Poyang of Liang.

sentences.zh: 該幼而謹厚，有譽鄉曲。

translations.literal: Gai from youth was careful and honest and had a reputation in his district.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was careful and honest from youth and was respected in his district.

sentences.zh: 尤善醫術，見稱於時。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in medical art and was praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in medicine and praised in his time.

sentences.zh: 仕梁，歷武陵王府參軍。

translations.literal: He served Liang, passing through the post of Adjutant in the household of the Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Liang as adjutant in the household of the Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 隨府西上。

translations.literal: He followed the princely household west.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the princely household west.

sentences.zh: 後與蕭撝同歸國，授平東將軍、左銀青光祿大夫，轉驃騎將軍、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he returned to the state together with Xiao Hou and was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Left Grand Master of the Silver Gate and Purple Radiance, then transferred to General of Agile Cavalry and Right Grand Master of Radiant Honor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned with Xiao Hou and was made general who pacifies the east and left grand master of the silver gate and purple radiance, then general of agile cavalry and right grand master of radiant honor.

sentences.zh: 武成元年，除醫正上士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wucheng he was appointed Senior Clerk, Chief Physician.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wucheng he was appointed senior clerk, chief physician.

sentences.zh: 自許奭死後，該稍為時人所重，賓客迎候，亞於姚僧垣。

translations.literal: After Xu Yi died, Gai was gradually valued by people of the age; guests who came to greet him were second only to Yao Sengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Yi died, Gai was gradually valued; guests sought him out second only to Yao Sengyuan.

sentences.zh: 天和初，遷縣伯下大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was promoted to Lower Grand Master of a district earl.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianhe he was promoted to lower grand master of a district earl.

sentences.zh: 五年，進授車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was advanced to General of Chariots and Cavalry and Palace Attendant of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was advanced to general of chariots and cavalry and palace attendant of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 該性淹和，不自矜尚，但有請之者，皆為盡其藝術。

translations.literal: Gai was mild and harmonious by nature and did not boast; whenever anyone requested him, he always exhausted his art.
translations.idiomatic: Gai was mild and unassuming; whenever anyone sought him he gave his full skill.

sentences.zh: 時論稱其長者焉。

translations.literal: Contemporaries called him a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called him a man of mature character.

sentences.zh: 後以疾卒。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He later died of illness.

sentences.zh: 子士則，亦傳其家業。

translations.literal: His son Shize also transmitted the family profession.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shize also carried on the family profession.

sentences.zh: 時有強練，不知何許人，亦不知其名字。

translations.literal: At the time there was Qiang Lian, of unknown origin, also unknown in name.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Qiang Lian, of unknown origin and unknown name.

sentences.zh: 魏時有李順興者，語默不恆，好言未然之事，當時號為李練。

translations.literal: In Wei there was one Li Shunxing, whose speech and silence were not constant; he loved to speak of things not yet happened, and the age called him Li Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei there was Li Shunxing, whose speech was erratic; he loved to speak of things not yet happened, and the age called him Li Lian.

sentences.zh: 世人以強類練，故亦呼為練焉。

translations.literal: People, because Qiang resembled Lian, also called him Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Because Qiang resembled him, people also called him Lian.

sentences.zh: 容貌長壯，有異於人。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and strong, different from other men.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and strong, unlike other men.

sentences.zh: 神精僘侃，莫之能測。

translations.literal: His spirit was wild and lofty; none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit was wild and lofty; none could fathom him.

sentences.zh: 意欲有所論說，逢人輒言。

translations.literal: When he wished to discourse, he spoke to whomever he met.
translations.idiomatic: When he wished to speak, he spoke to whomever he met.

sentences.zh: 若值其不欲言，縱苦加祈請，亦不相酬答。

translations.literal: If he did not wish to speak, even if one bitterly entreated him, he would not respond.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not wish to speak, even earnest pleading won no answer.

sentences.zh: 初聞其言，略不可解。

translations.literal: At first hearing his words, they could barely be understood.
translations.idiomatic: At first hearing, his words could barely be understood.

sentences.zh: 事過之後，往往有驗。

translations.literal: After the events passed, they were often verified.
translations.idiomatic: After events passed, they were often verified.

sentences.zh: 恆寄住諸佛寺，好遊行民家，兼歷造王公邸第。

translations.literal: He constantly lodged in various Buddhist temples, loved to travel among common households, and also went to the mansions of kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He lodged in Buddhist temples, visited common households, and also went to the mansions of kings and dukes.

sentences.zh: 所至之處，人皆敬而信之。

translations.literal: Wherever he arrived, people all revered and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he went, people revered and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 晉公護未誅之前，曾手持一大瓠，到護第門外，抵而破之。

translations.literal: Before Duke of Jin Hu was executed, he once held a large gourd, came to the gate outside Hu's mansion, struck it and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Before Duke Hu was executed, Qiang Lian once took a large gourd to the gate of Hu's mansion and smashed it.

sentences.zh: 乃大言曰：「瓠破子苦。

translations.literal: He then cried out loudly, "The gourd is broken—the sons will suffer.
translations.idiomatic: He cried out, "The gourd is broken—the sons will suffer."

sentences.zh: 」時柱國、平高公侯伏侯龍恩早依隨護，深被任委。

translations.literal: " At that time the pillar of state, Duke of Pinggao Hou Fuhou Long'en, had long followed Hu and was deeply entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Long'en, pillar of state and Duke of Pinggao, had long served Hu and enjoyed his deep trust.

sentences.zh: 強練至龍恩宅，呼其妻元氏及其妾媵並婢僕等，並令連席而坐。

translations.literal: Qiang Lian came to Long'en's house, called his wife Lady Yuan and his concubines and maidservants and the like, and ordered them all to sit on connected mats together.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian came to Long'en's house and summoned his wife Lady Yuan, his concubines, maidservants, and the rest, ordering them all to sit together on one mat.

sentences.zh: 諸人以逼夫人，苦辭不肯。

translations.literal: The others, because the lady was being compelled, bitterly declined and would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: They protested that the lady of the house was being forced and refused.

sentences.zh: 強練曰：「汝等一例人耳，何有貴賤。

translations.literal: Qiang Lian said, "You are all the same kind of people—what is there of noble and base?
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian said, "You are all the same kind of people. What difference is there between high and low?"

sentences.zh: 」遂逼就坐。

translations.literal: " He then compelled them to take their seats.
translations.idiomatic: He forced them to sit.

sentences.zh: 未幾而護誅，諸子並死。

translations.literal: Before long Hu was executed and all his sons died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hu was executed and all his sons died with him.

sentences.zh: 龍恩亦伏法，仍籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Long'en also suffered execution, and his household was moreover confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Long'en was executed as well, and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 建德中，每夜上街衢邊樹，大哭釋迦牟尼佛，或至申旦，如此者累日，聲甚哀憐。

translations.literal: In the Jiande era, each night he went to a tree by the street and wept greatly for Shakyamuni Buddha, sometimes until the fifth watch; this continued for days, and his voice was very piteous.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiande era he went each night to a tree by the street and wailed for Shakyamuni Buddha, sometimes until dawn, for days on end, in a voice full of pity.

sentences.zh: 俄而廢佛、道二教。

translations.literal: Before long the two teachings of Buddhism and Daoism were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long both Buddhism and Daoism were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 大象末，又以一無底囊，歷長安市肆告乞，市人爭以米麥遺之。

translations.literal: At the end of Daxiang, again with a bottomless sack he went through the markets of Chang'an begging; market people vied to give him rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he took a bottomless sack through the markets of Chang'an begging, and people vied to give him grain.

sentences.zh: 強練張囊投之，隨卽漏之於地。

translations.literal: Qiang Lian opened the sack to receive it, and it immediately leaked to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian held the sack open to receive the grain, and it immediately spilled to the ground.

sentences.zh: 人或問之曰：「汝何為也？

translations.literal: Someone asked him, "What are you doing?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked him, "What are you doing?"

sentences.zh: 」強練曰：「此亦無餘，但欲使諸人見盛空耳。

translations.literal: " Qiang Lian said, "This too leaves nothing over—I only wish to let everyone see fullness become empty.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Nothing remains—I only want everyone to see fullness become empty."

sentences.zh: 」至隋開皇初，果移都于龍首山，長安城遂空廢。

translations.literal: " By the beginning of Kaihuang under Sui, the capital was indeed moved to Longshou Mountain, and the city of Chang'an was left empty and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang under the Sui the capital was indeed moved to Longshou Mountain, and Chang'an was left empty.

sentences.zh: 後亦莫知其所終。

translations.literal: Later no one knew his end.
translations.idiomatic: Later no one knew what became of him.

sentences.zh: 又有蜀郡衛元嵩者，亦好言將來之事，蓋江左寶志之流。

translations.literal: There was also Wei Yuansong of Shu Commandery, who likewise loved to speak of things to come—of the same sort as Baozhi of the Jiang left.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Wei Yuansong of Shu commandery, who likewise loved to speak of the future—much like Baozhi of the southern dynasties.

sentences.zh: 天和中，著詩預論周、隋廢興及皇家受命，並有徵驗。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he composed poems foretelling the rise and fall of Zhou and Sui and the receiving of the mandate by the imperial house—all were verified.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianhe era he wrote poems foretelling the fall of Zhou and Sui and the rise of the new dynasty, all of which were later verified.

sentences.zh: 性尤不信釋教，嘗上疏極論之。

translations.literal: By nature he especially did not believe in the Buddhist teaching and once submitted a memorial arguing against it to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He especially disbelieved Buddhism and once submitted a memorial arguing against it at length.

sentences.zh: 史失其事，故不為傳。

translations.literal: The history has lost his affairs, and therefore no biography is made.
translations.idiomatic: The histories have lost his record, and so no biography is given here.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：仁義之於教，大矣，術藝之於用，博矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Benevolence and righteousness in teaching are great; arts and skills in use are broad.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Benevolence and righteousness in teaching are great matters; arts and skills in practice are broad fields.

sentences.zh: 狥於是者，不能無非，厚於利者，必有其害。

translations.literal: Those who pursue these cannot be without fault; those who are thick toward profit must have their harm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pursue them cannot be without fault; those who prize profit too highly must suffer harm.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《書》、《禮》、《樂》所失也淺，故先王重其德。

translations.literal: The Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music—what is lost in them is shallow; therefore the former kings valued their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Odes, Documents, Rites, and Music what is lost is slight; therefore the former kings valued their moral power.

sentences.zh: 方術技巧，所失也深，故往哲輕其藝。

translations.literal: Methods, techniques, and craft skills—what is lost in them is deep; therefore sages of old slighted their arts.
translations.idiomatic: In methods, techniques, and craft what is lost runs deep; therefore sages of old held their arts lightly.

sentences.zh: 夫能通方術而不詭於俗，習技巧而必蹈於禮者，豈非大雅君子乎。

translations.literal: Now those who can master methods without being perverse toward custom, who practice skills yet always tread in ritual—is this not the great refined gentleman?
translations.idiomatic: Those who master these arts without perversity toward custom, who practice skills yet always keep to ritual—are they not true gentlemen of refinement?

sentences.zh: 姚僧垣診候精審，名冠於一代，其所全濟，固亦多焉。

translations.literal: Yao Sengyuan's examination and observation were precise and careful; his fame crowned a generation, and those he fully saved were indeed many.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sengyuan's diagnoses were precise and careful; his fame crowned his generation, and the lives he saved were many indeed.

sentences.zh: 而弘茲義方，皆為令器，故能享眉壽，縻好爵。

translations.literal: Moreover, by spreading this moral teaching, all became fine vessels; therefore they could enjoy long life and be tied to good ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By spreading this moral teaching they all became men of worth; therefore they enjoyed long life and held fine titles.

sentences.zh: 老聃云「天道無親，常與善人」，於是信矣。

translations.literal: Laozi said, "Heaven's Way has no favorites; it is constantly with the good person"—here it is believed.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi said, "The Way of Heaven has no favorites; it constantly aids the good"—here that is proved true.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses as its collation standard the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Zhou, November 1971.
